title: Tate-source identities in the derived category of strict reduction systems
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, with $g_{T,\gamma}=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius $\gamma$ [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Work at $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ with the completed derived operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and with actual derived coefficient systems and their derived reduction functor $\mathcal R_T$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A strict input datum means the specified realized-tower isomorphism of [def-pur-tate-datum]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated and finite type, with geometric base change smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$, and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ with such a datum. Use one flat-term K-flat representative for every simultaneous reduction, and the prescribed canonical comparisons, whose descent is [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] and whose composition is [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition]. The identities for $b$, for the canonical Tate arrows, and for the defining source composite $(Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d)[2d]b_{f,K}$ under coefficient quotients, Cartesian pullback of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and composition of smooth geometric base changes of dimensions $d,e\ge0$ hold as equalities of natural transformations in the derived category of actual coefficient systems, before derived inverse limit. Here $b$ is the source comparison of [def-pur-tate-datum]; the identities are those precisely stated in [lem-pur-finite-tate-source-structural-coherence], [lem-pur-canonical-tate-arrow-naturality], [lem-pur-finite-tate-source-comparison-calculus] and [lem-pur-iterated-tate-source-composite], interpreted simultaneously on the strict reductions. Their evaluations are the corresponding finite comparisons, with the integral-to-finite comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; applying the functorial derived inverse limit gives the integral equations. The identities are natural for all morphisms of the realized derived input systems, including the specified datum; no lifting or uniqueness of a system map from its separate derived evaluations is asserted.

proof.text: Put $N=\mathcal R_YK$ and retain the specified arrow $\varphi:G_YN\cong N$ as an arrow of derived systems. Use the sequence-site equivalence to regard strict coefficient systems as modules over the ring sheaf $(n,U)\mapsto(A_{E,n})_Y(U)$. A scheme pullback acts on the $U$ coordinate and leaves $n$ fixed; a coefficient quotient acts by the ring quotient. Hence their structural ring maps commute. Apply the ringed-topos monoidal comparison theorem on these small sequence sites. It supplies tensor comparisons and monoidal pullback-composition comparisons natural for every morphism in the derived system categories. The finite-system composition theorem fixes the normalization: its maps are the termwise module comparisons and its associativity equation already holds before localization. In particular $c_f:G_XF_f\cong F_fG_Y$ is the comparison for the actual equality $fg_X=g_Yf$ on these sites, not a map reconstructed from its evaluations.

proof.text: Write $T_r$ for the strict Tate system and $P_fN=(F_fN\otimes T_d)[2d]$. Form $b_f=(c_f\otimes1)[2d]\mu_{g_X}[2d]$ on systems. To compare it with a coefficient quotient or a Cartesian pullback $Q$, expand both routes $QG_XP_fN\to H'_{f'}Q_YN$ in this formula. Naturality of $\mu$ moves the comparison for $Q$ past the tensorator; monoidality of pullback composition moves it past $c_f$. The two expansions then have the same pullback-composition and scalar-association maps, giving $a_HQ_X(b_f)=b'_{f'}G'_X(a_P)C_X$. For three composable pullbacks, apply the composition equation for the tensorator and associativity of the composition maps: expansion first through $b_f,F_f(b_h)$ equals expansion through $b_{hf}$. These are system equations: on the simultaneous flat-term models the cochain coefficient-change squares commute with every quotient transition, and strict tower coherence gives the associator, unit and composition equations before localization. Shift is termwise reindexing; the only interchanges here involve even shifts and degree-zero twists and have sign $1$.

proof.text: For the canonical Tate arrows apply the strict-system clause of Tate-arrow naturality: $t_QQ(\tau_r)=\tau'_rG'(t_Q)C_Q$, for spatial pullback and coefficient reduction. Write $\alpha_{r,s}:T_r\otimes^LT_s\cong T_{r+s}$. Its additivity equation is $\alpha_{r,s}(\tau_r\otimes^L\tau_s)\mu_g=\tau_{r+s}G(\alpha_{r,s})$. For spatial $w:T'\to T$ retain the typed mixed equation: with $\tau_s^w=F_w(\tau_{s,T})C_{w,T_{s,T}}^{-1}$ and $a_{w,r,s}=\alpha_{r,s,T'}(1\otimes^Lt_{w,s})$, it is $a_{w,r,s}(\tau_{r,T'}\otimes^L\tau_s^w)\mu_{g_{T'}}=\tau_{r+s,T'}G_{T'}(a_{w,r,s})$. Here $C_w:F_wG_T\cong G_{T'}F_w$, so both sides start at $G_{T'}(T_{r,T'}\otimes^LF_wT_{s,T})$ and end at $T_{r+s,T'}$. These are equations on the compatible roots-of-unity systems themselves, including the coefficient-unit case $r=0$, not lifts of separately specified finite arrows.

proof.text: Set $A_f=(F_f\varphi\otimes\tau_d)[2d]$ and $\psi_f=A_fb_f$. Naturality of the pullback-tensor comparison in the system arrow $\varphi$, together with Step 3, gives $a_PQ_X(A_f)=A'_{f'}a_H$, where $\varphi'=Q_Y(\varphi)C_Y^{-1}$. Multiply Step 2 on the left by $A'_{f'}$: $a_PQ_X(\psi_f)=A'_{f'}b'_{f'}G'_X(a_P)C_X$. This is the required source-composite equation for quotients and Cartesian pullback, with the same $a_P,a_H,C$ as above. Only functoriality, tensor naturality and cancellation of $C_Y^{-1}C_Y$ occur in this pasting.

proof.text: For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow hZ$ expand $\psi_{f,h}=(F_f((F_h\varphi\otimes\tau_e)[2e]b_h)\otimes\tau_d)[2d]b_f$. Move $F_f(b_h)$ through the tensor comparison by naturality and apply Step 2. The initial structural map becomes the expansion of $b_{hf}G_X(J)$; naturality of pullback composition identifies the input arrow with $F_{hf}\varphi$. On the two twist factors use the mixed equation of Step 3 with $w=f,r=d,s=e$, not an untyped product of arrows on different schemes. Put $\tau_e^f=F_f(\tau_{e,Y})C_{f,T_{e,Y}}^{-1}$ and $a=\alpha_{d,e,X}(1\otimes^Lt_{f,e})$. If $\sigma:F_fT_{e,Y}\otimes^LT_{d,X}\cong T_{d,X}\otimes^LF_fT_{e,Y}$, put $\beta=a\sigma$, the twist part of $J$. Monoidality of symmetry changes the mixed equation to $\beta(\tau_e^f\otimes^L\tau_{d,X})\mu_{g_X}=\tau_{d+e,X}G_X(\beta)$. Substituting it into the expansion gives $J\psi_{f,h}=(F_{hf}\varphi\otimes\tau_{d+e,X})[2(d+e)]b_{hf}G_X(J)$ as an equation of system arrows. For $d=0$ or $e=0$ the same equations use the coefficient unit. The twists have degree zero and both shifts are even, so their interchange has sign $1$.

proof.text: Evaluate these system transformations at $n$. The representative tensor maps are $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, and composition is the finite module-pullback comparison. Thus the evaluations are precisely the prescribed finite $b$-coherence, Tate-arrow, source-composite and iterated-source comparisons, with the equations stated in the four finite-calculus nodes. In the iterated formula the twist identification is the typed mixed equation with $C_f^{-1}$ and $t_{f,e}$ from Steps 3 and 5; it does not identify arrows with different domains. The operation-reduction theorem identifies the integral-to-finite comparisons with these prescribed pullback, tensor and unit comparisons on their finite-Tor domains. No assertion here treats evaluation as faithful on morphisms: the equalities were proved on systems in Steps 2--5.

proof.text: Apply $\mathcal L_X=R\lim\,U_X$ to the system equations. This is a functor, so it preserves their composites and equalities. Completed-operation substitution identifies the limit of every whole pullback/tensor expression with the completed expression, naturally in all input system maps and compatibly with substitution. The well-definedness theorem fixes independence of the simultaneous flat-term representatives; the integral pullback-composition theorem identifies the resulting composition maps with the prescribed ones. Termwise shifts commute with this exact derived-limit functor. Conjugating by these comparisons gives the asserted integral equations. Every comparison used above is natural on derived systems, so the argument also applies to every morphism respecting the specified datum, without requiring a chain representative for that datum on the originally chosen integral resolution.
